title: Moonwalker Descending Neurons Mediate Visually Evoked Retreat in Drosophila.
source_locator: Abstract (Europe PMC; full text not accessible)
quote: Here, we present data from functional imaging, behavioral epistasis, and unilateral activation experiments that support these hypotheses.
mapping_basis: The paper's name MDN (moonwalker descending neuron) is itself the MANC type name in assigned_types.csv.
notes: Abstract only; full text was blocked (403/captcha) at the publisher, PMC and Europe PMC, and bioRxiv has no preprint. The hypothesis supported is 'turning while walking backward might reflect asymmetric activation of the left and right MDNs', so unilateral MDN activation implies backward walking with turning, coded yes for all legs per PROTOCOL 3. The effector, its kind (optogenetic is a placeholder because the schema requires one), the driver line, stimulation and preparation (free or tethered) are not stated in the abstract. Bilateral MDN activation causing backward walking is cited from the authors' earlier work [19], not tested here, so it gets no record.
